C2-01.title: Where do you serve?
C2-01.scene: You're serving from the right. Your partner is at the net on the left.
C2-01.cue: Your partner is in the middle of the box, eyeing the middle.
C2-01.question: Where do you serve?

answer.why: It gives the returner the narrowest angles. A return through the middle is your partner's to pick off.
answer.caption: Your partner picked it off

lo.why: It pulls the returner out — but it opens up the return angles too.
lo.caption: The return angles opened up

hi.short: Short and slow, just to be safe
hi.why: A short serve just to get it in lets the returner step in and attack.
hi.caption: Too short — attacked

C2-01.coach: A serve down the T funnels the ball to your partner.
C2-01.next: After a wide serve, where does the return go?

C2-02.title: Wide serve: where's the return going?
C2-02.scene: Your partner hit a wide serve from the left.
C2-02.cue: The returner is being pulled wide.
C2-02.question: Where will the return go?

answer.why: A stretched returner usually plays the safe crosscourt, and that ball passes through the middle.
answer.caption: You read it and picked it off

lo.why: It could happen. But backing off early throws away your chance to pick it off.
lo.caption: The crosscourt got past

hi.why: From that stretched spot, down the line rarely works. Guarding your alley opens the middle.
hi.caption: It slipped through the middle

C2-02.coach: A stretched returner's ball comes through the middle.
C2-02.next: After a body serve, do you poach?

C2-03.title: After a body serve: poach or not?
C2-03.scene: Your partner's serve jammed the returner.
C2-03.cue: The returner twists and gets the racket up.
C2-03.question: What do you do?

answer.why: Off a jamming serve, they're just trying to block it back. The floater comes through the middle.
answer.caption: You cut off the floater

lo.why: Safe, but you let the floater through the middle go by.
lo.caption: Your partner barely gets it

hi.why: A blocked return is short and slow. If you back off, you can't reach the ball dropping in front.
hi.caption: It just dropped in front of you

C2-03.coach: After a jamming serve, it's time to poach.

C2-04.title: The fake poach
C2-04.scene: The returner keeps hitting easy crosscourt returns. No chance to poach.
C2-04.cue: This serve, too, the returner is waiting comfortably.
C2-04.question: What do you do?

answer.short: Show a half step to the middle
answer.why: If you fake a move, the returner is tempted to switch to down the line. Wait for that ball.
answer.caption: You caught the down-the-line

lo.why: Safe, but the returner keeps hitting comfortable crosscourts.
lo.caption: The easy crosscourts keep coming

hi.why: The returner sees everything. Leave early and they'll hit down the empty line.
hi.caption: Beaten down the empty line

C2-04.coach: If you can't poach, just show it.
C2-04.next: What if the ball went low?

C2-05.title: Punish the net player who always poaches
C2-05.scene: The opposing net player has poached three times in a row.
C2-05.cue: The net player is heading for the middle again.
C2-05.question: Where do you return it?

answer.short: Down the line they left open
answer.why: A net player who always goes middle leaves the line open. Show it once and they'll stop leaving.
answer.caption: Through the empty line

lo.short: Hard at the net player's feet
lo.why: Their feet are a good target, but a net player on the move can still block it.
lo.caption: The net player barely blocks it

hi.why: That's exactly the lane the net player just ran into.
hi.caption: Cut off by the poach

C2-05.coach: A net player who keeps leaving gets one down the line.
C2-05.next: What if the net player changes position?

C2-06.title: Returning a big first serve
C2-06.scene: A fast first serve came to your backhand.
C2-06.cue: No time for a big swing.
C2-06.question: Where do you return it?

answer.why: Even a small block has pace on it. Sending it deep to the server keeps it away from the net player.
answer.caption: Blocked it back deep

lo.why: It gets over. But lobbing a fast serve tends to fall short.
lo.caption: The lob was short

hi.why: Adding power to a fast ball sends it long. And the net is higher there.
hi.caption: It sailed long

C2-06.coach: Don't swing at a fast serve — block it.
C2-06.next: What if it's still too fast?

C2-07.title: A big first serve: move back to return?
C2-07.scene: The first serve is fast. You've already missed two.
C2-07.cue: The ball is past before your racket gets there.
C2-07.question: Where do you return from?

answer.why: Against a fast serve, distance is time. Moving back gives you time to get your racket on it.
answer.caption: Got it back properly

lo.why: You can return it, but you'll be late and the ball floats.
lo.caption: Late — the ball floated

hi.why: That's your second-serve spot. Stepping into a fast serve makes it go by even faster.
hi.caption: Couldn't even touch it

C2-07.coach: Fast serves from further back, slow serves from further in.

C2-08.title: Where to return a second serve
C2-08.cue: The opposing net player is still in the middle of the box.
C2-08.question: Where do you send it?

answer.why: Even on a chance ball, don't force it. Go deep, push the server back, and we're ahead.
answer.caption: Pushed the server back

lo.why: A good shot, but with the net player standing there, it's within reach.
lo.caption: It was in the net player's reach

hi.why: The net player can reach it just by stretching. And the net is highest there.
hi.caption: The net player just reached out

C2-08.coach: The better the chance, the deeper crosscourt — then move in.
C2-08.next: You hit it deep — how far do you go?

C2-09.title: After the second-serve return: how far in?
C2-09.scene: Your return went deep into the server's corner.
C2-09.cue: The server got pushed behind the baseline.
C2-09.question: How far in do you go?

answer.why: A pushed-back server floats the ball. Stop at the service line and you can handle a floater or a lob.
answer.caption: You volleyed the floater

lo.why: Safe, but you let the moment slip while they're pushed back.
lo.caption: You let the chance go

hi.short: All the way to the net at once
hi.why: The ball arrives while you're still running, and the pushed server lobs over your head.
hi.caption: It went over your head

C2-09.coach: Once you've pushed them back, move up to the service line.
C2-09.next: Your first volley after moving in?

C2-10.title: Serve and volley: where do you stop?
C2-10.scene: You serve and run straight in toward the net.
C2-10.cue: The returner is starting the backswing.
C2-10.question: Where do you stop?

answer.why: Pause as the returner hits (a split step). Then you can go after a ball either way.
answer.caption: You hit the first volley deep

lo.short: Stop after just a few steps
lo.why: Stopping is right. But you're too far back, so the ball bounces at your feet.
lo.caption: You barely dig it out

hi.why: If the ball comes while you're running, you can't change direction. It goes past you.
hi.caption: It slipped past you

C2-10.coach: Stop when they hit, then move in again.
C2-10.next: What about from the returner's side?

C2-11.title: Your return went deep — move in?
C2-11.scene: Your return went deep. But the server had already backed up.
C2-11.cue: The server is set for a big swing.
C2-11.question: Where do you go?

answer.why: It was deep, but the server was waiting comfortably. A hard ball is coming, so take it from the back.
answer.caption: You handled the hard ball

lo.short: Move in two or three steps
lo.why: That's no man's land. A deep ball bounces at your feet.
lo.caption: You barely handle the bounce

hi.short: Go all the way to the net
hi.why: A ball hit comfortably comes back fast and low. It drops at your feet while you're running.
hi.caption: It landed at your feet

C2-11.coach: Only move in when they're pushed back.
C2-11.next: Your first volley after moving in?

C2-12.title: A low return at your feet: where to?
C2-12.scene: The return came low and deep, right at your feet.
C2-12.cue: The opposing net player is waiting in the middle of the box.
C2-12.question: Where do you hit it?

answer.why: You have to hit up on a ball at your feet. Send it deep crosscourt, farthest from the net player.
answer.caption: You lifted it deep and held on

lo.why: A good idea, but it's hard to lob deep off a ball at your feet.
lo.caption: The net player backs up and gets it

hi.why: Hitting hard from your feet makes the ball float — right at the net player's racket height.
hi.caption: The net player picked it off

C2-12.coach: From your feet: lift it high and deep.

C2-13.title: A floated return: where to put it away?
C2-13.scene: The return floated high. Both opponents backed up.
C2-13.cue: They're side by side on the baseline.
C2-13.question: Where do you hit it?

answer.why: When both are back, the middle is the safest way to attack. They hesitate over who takes it.
answer.caption: It went through the middle

lo.why: Safe, but you turned a chance ball into an ordinary one.
lo.caption: It became an ordinary rally

hi.why: The better the chance, the bigger the target. The corner is small and easy to miss.
hi.caption: Went for the corner — out

C2-13.coach: When they're both back, go down the middle.

C2-14.title: You kept it low — one more step
C2-14.scene: Your volley landed at the feet of the returner coming in.
C2-14.cue: The returner bends and lifts the ball.
C2-14.question: What do you do?

answer.short: One more step to the middle
answer.why: If you kept it low, the lifted ball is coming. Step in to the middle and finish it from above.
answer.caption: Finished it a step closer

lo.why: Not bad, but you take the floater from down low.
lo.caption: You just get it back over

hi.why: A lifted ball is short and slow. Back off and it drops in front of you.
hi.caption: You couldn't reach the short ball

C2-14.coach: If you kept it low, take one more step in.

C2-15.title: We floated it — what do you do?
C2-15.scene: Your partner's third ball floated high — but it's deep.
C2-15.cue: The returner is getting ready to hit at shoulder height.
C2-15.question: What do you do?

answer.short: Back off to the service line
answer.why: It's a deep floater, so no immediate smash. From the service line you can handle a hard ball.
answer.caption: You stepped back and blocked it

lo.short: All the way to the baseline
lo.why: Safe, but you went too far back. You give up the front to a short ball.
lo.caption: You barely reach the short ball

hi.why: Off a floater, the returner drives it hard at the net player. The closer you are, the harder it is.
hi.caption: Drilled at your feet

C2-15.coach: Against a deep floater, back off only to the service line.
C2-15.next: What if a lob goes over your head?

C2-16.title: Their net player poached
C2-16.cue: The opposing net player charges the middle and cuts it off.
C2-16.question: What do you do?

answer.why: A poached ball goes through the middle between you. Cover the middle first.
answer.caption: You blocked it and counterattacked

lo.why: It buys time, but you can't reach a ball that drops short.
lo.caption: You barely scooped it up

hi.why: Standing still and watching, you can't move for a ball at your feet. That's where the poach goes.
hi.caption: Drilled at your feet

C2-16.coach: When their net player moves, close in to the middle.
C2-16.next: What if you blocked the poach?

C2-17.title: You blocked the poach
C2-17.scene: The opposing net player poached, and the ball is coming to you.
C2-17.cue: The right side where the net player was is now empty.
C2-17.question: Where do you block it?

answer.short: To the side the net player left
answer.why: The poaching net player is in the middle. Nobody can get back to their spot.
answer.caption: Sent it back into the gap

lo.why: Safe, but you leave the net player's empty spot alone.
lo.caption: The rally goes on

hi.short: Straight back at the net player
hi.why: Send it to the net player's racket again and it gets cut off again.
hi.caption: Cut off again

C2-17.coach: Block a poach to the side the net player left.
C2-17.next: What if you face the I formation?

C2-18.title: First volley after the return
C2-18.scene: You returned and came up toward the service line. The server hits low.
C2-18.cue: The ball skims the net and comes at your feet.
C2-18.question: Where do you hit it from, and where to?

answer.why: Stop at the service line and send the low ball deep. Then close in on the net.
answer.caption: Sent it deep, then closed in

lo.why: Backing off is safe, but you throw away the chance the return gave you.
lo.caption: You missed the chance

hi.short: Run all the way to the net
hi.why: Hitting a low ball on the run makes it float — and their net player is waiting.
hi.caption: Hit by the floater

C2-18.coach: First volley: stop, and hit it deep.

C2-19.title: A lobbed return — the switch call
C2-19.scene: The return is a lob floating over your head. Not very deep.
C2-19.cue: It looks like it'll land near the service line.
C2-19.question: What do you do?

answer.short: Back up and smash it yourself
answer.why: The net player takes a short lob by backing up — faster than your partner running over.
answer.caption: You backed up and hit it

lo.why: Not wrong, but your partner has to run a long way for a short ball.
lo.caption: Your partner barely gets it back

hi.why: If nobody calls it, you both freeze — and it drops between you.
hi.caption: You both froze

C2-19.coach: Short lob: you take it. Deep lob: switch.
C2-19.next: Your new spots after the switch?

C2-20.title: New spots after the switch: who goes where
C2-20.scene: After the switch, your partner's lob went deep over the opponents.
C2-20.question: Where do you go?

answer.short: A half step toward the middle
answer.why: The right is your side now. Closing toward the middle lets you cut off the ball coming back.
answer.caption: You finished the ball that came back

lo.why: The sideline angle is narrow. You'll be late on a ball through the middle.
lo.caption: Your partner covers for you

hi.short: Go back to your old left side
hi.why: Your partner is already on the left. The whole right is open.
hi.caption: The right was open

C2-20.coach: After a switch, your new spot is yours.

C2-21.title: Facing the Australian formation
C2-21.scene: The opposing net player is at the net on the same side as the server.
C2-21.cue: Their net player is right in your crosscourt lane.
C2-21.question: Where do you return it?

answer.why: Block the crosscourt and the line opens up. The server has to run.
answer.caption: Into the open line

lo.why: The middle is between the net player and the server. Either one can reach it.
lo.caption: The server gets it back

hi.why: The net player is standing right in that lane. It gets cut off.
hi.caption: Cut off by the net player

C2-21.coach: When they block the crosscourt, the line opens.

C2-22.title: The I formation: where will they go?
C2-22.scene: The server is near the middle; the net player is crouched at the center of the net.
C2-22.cue: As the serve goes in, the net player stands up.
C2-22.question: Who do you watch now?

answer.why: In this formation, everything depends on which way the net player goes. Watch their first step.
answer.caption: You watched the net player and blocked it

lo.why: After serving, the server goes opposite the net player. The net player moves first.
lo.caption: A beat late

hi.why: Watch only the ball and you miss the net player's move. The volley comes at your feet.
hi.caption: Drilled at your feet

C2-22.coach: Against the I formation, watch the crouching net player.

C2-23.title: Plan through the third ball
C2-23.scene: You served down the T. The returner takes it in the middle.
C2-23.cue: The returner is standing in the middle of the court.
C2-23.question: Where do you hit the third ball from?

answer.why: Returns off a T serve come through the middle. Be there early and hit it deep.
answer.caption: You sent the third ball deep

lo.why: Not bad, but you're a step late on a return down the middle.
lo.caption: You run and barely hit it

hi.why: Planning the third ball starts behind the baseline. Move in and the return lands at your feet.
hi.caption: It landed at your feet

C2-23.coach: Serve down the T, play the third ball from the middle.

C2-24.title: Chapter 2 review
C2-24.scene: Your partner's ball landed at the feet of an opponent coming forward.
C2-24.cue: The opponent bends and gets the racket under it.
C2-24.question: How will the next ball come?

answer.why: They have to lift a ball at their feet, so it floats slowly. You finish it in the middle.
answer.caption: You finished the floater

lo.why: It could. But leaving the floater to your partner lets the chance slip.
lo.caption: Your partner gets it back

hi.short: Hard down the line, beside you
hi.why: It's hard to drive a lifted ball down the line. Guard your side and the middle opens.
hi.caption: It went through the middle

C2-24.coach: If you hit it at their feet, wait for the floater.
